media.alt: Ten per cent children in Karachi are asthmatic, exclusive breastfeeding may prevent asthma

content.text: "Exclusive breastfeeding has been demonstrated to reduce the incidence of childhood asthma," revealed Dr Naseeruddin Mahmood, Consultant Paediatrician, the Aga Khan University (AKU). He was speaking at the First Childhood Asthma Seminar and Workshop held at AKU on Wednesday May 3, 2000.

The seminar's objective was to increase awareness of childhood asthma amongst physicians, introduce new methods of treatment and dispel the myths and misunderstandings surrounding the disease. A workshop followed the seminar, providing hands-on training on necessary skills, such as giving oxygen, nebulization and the correct usage of inhalers for asthmatic children.

Asthma is a chronic disease, triggering repeated illnesses and leading to a poor quality of life and maybe even fatal. However, it is being under-diagnosed and under-treated, particularly in children who are suffering from it in increasing numbers. This is mainly due to the lack of awareness about childhood asthma amongst doctors.

Professor Zulfiqar A. Bhutta, Professor of Paediatrics and Child Health, AKU, presented data showing that asthma is increasing in Pakistan. He stated that about 10% children in Karachi are currently suffering from asthma and the number is likely to increase in the future. Several speakers also emphasized the role of passive smoking, dust-mites, artificial food colors and family history as significant risk-factors.

Professor A. Gaffar Billoo Chairman and Professor, Department of Paediatrics, AKU, highlighted the need to educate parents to alleviate their fears about the disease. He stated that the anxiety of being labeled an asthmatic harms patients, and urged physicians to take up the role of educators to dispel the public's misconceptions and fears.
